summary: Kenji Watanabe is an Indologist who studied under Jozef Deleu. In 1978, he was attested holding the post of assistant (副手) at Taisho University.

Kenjiu Kasawara (1851–1883) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, studying under Friedrich Max Müller from 1879 to 1882 and Arthur Anthony Macdonell around 1880 to 1882.

Kennard Lipman works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther and held a post as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.
Kenneth Doo Young Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe and held an attested post at Stetson University in 2007.

Kenneth G. Zysk is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He earned an M.A. at UC Santa Barbara and a Ph.D. at Australian National University, holding posts at UCLA, Eastern Michigan University (attested 1989), and the University of Copenhagen (attested 2012).

Kenneth J. Guest is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He studied at Columbia University, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, and CUNY (PhD) under Aloysius Pieris, and held posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under Wagiswara. He served as Professor of the History of Religion at the Pacific School of Religion (circa 1921–1935) and as a lecturer at UC.

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and served as chair of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (1996–1999).

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1984–1998) and Musashino University (~1998–2018).

Kenneth Roy Norman (1925–2020) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Downing College. He held positions at the Pali Text Society (President in 1988), the University of Cambridge, and SOAS.

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1979–1989). He held positions at Rissho University, Eastern Institute, Aichi Gakuin University (~1999–2010), and became a professor at the University of Tokyo in 2010.
Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a doctorate in literature at Otani University. He is attested as professor emeritus at Hanazono University in 2014.
Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa (1888–1969) studied at Bukkyo University, specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Ryukoku University (~1928–1958) and Bukkyo University (~1950–1960), and founded the Tantric Buddhism Research Society in 1960.
Kenshi Kusano is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from ~1971 to 1980 and served as a professor there from ~1999 to 2018.
Kensuke Nedachi is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1976 to 1983 and later served as a professor there from ~2006 to 2022.

Kenta Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University (~1994–1998) and the University of Tokyo (~1998–2005). He became an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College around 2012.

Kenyu Mitomo is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley under Akira Hirakawa and others. He held multiple leadership and professorial roles at Rissho University between ~1974 and 2016.

Kevin A. Vose is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his B.A. at Bates College and his M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins and Ngawang Jinpa.
Kevin Buckelew is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Sarah Lawrence College. His doctoral supervisors included Chun-fang Yu, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.
